clue.text: Article in card misprinted in test: marks deducted officially

indicators.note: the whole article-and-card unit goes in the shortened test word
deducted says the letter for marks is taken away from the test word

parts.note: an exam is a test
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: the article sits in the scrambled card
a misprinted word has its letters jumbled, so the letters of card are rearranged

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An exam paper carries a misprinted card, and marks are officially docked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misprinted' rearranges the card letters to CADR, which holds the article; 'marks deducted' trims the test to EXA, round the lot. Marks are M, the old German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'from the chair', the phrase describes a pronouncement made with full authority, as by a pope or bishop.

clue.text: German carrying cover for aircraft

indicators.note: the German abbreviation carries the cover within it

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A German man carries a cover for an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineless winged craft that rides air currents is a kind of aircraft.

clue.text: A quantity of salt water may be treated with ease

indicators.note: treated letters are processed into a new form, so with and ease are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seawater can be handled easily, as if describing a purification process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be treated' rearranges the letters of WITH and EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an inlet of the Barents Sea in northern Russia, so a body of salt water.

clue.text: Trust edition will be included in review

indicators.note: the edition abbreviation goes inside the review word

parts.note: a crit is a critical review

explanation.surface: A publisher trusts that a new edition will be reviewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone credit means believing them, so the noun is a synonym for belief or faith.

clue.text: Toilet staff restricting hot water? There's a way out

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: the staff hems in the letter for hot

parts.note: a pole is a staff or rod
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a toilet with a broken pipe looks for an escape from the hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot water' also suggests trouble, which is what an escape clause gets you out of; 'water?' adds to that picture and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap in a rule that lets someone evade it is an escape route, an exit.

clue.text: Key point that's the conclusion of many a scientific expert?

definitions.meaning: the essential substance or main thrust of something

definitions.text: the conclusion of many a scientific expert
definitions.meaning: the ending shared by biologist, geologist and other names for specialists

explanation.surface: What a scientist's findings boil down to.
explanation.definitionFit: The core meaning of an argument is its substance, and the same four letters end many words for scientists.

clue.text: What skater may do — cut line?

parts.note: to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: A question about whether a skater cuts across the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure skater may perform a jump with one and a half rotations named after Axel Paulsen.

clue.text: Theatrical fellow's a lively guy, bringing in King and I

parts.note: a fellow's things are his

indicators.note: the tonic takes in the king's letter and I

parts.note: someone invigorating is said to be a real tonic
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A cheerful man's showiness draws in a monarch and the speaker, like a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' is a stage musical, which feeds the theatrical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdone and melodramatic behaviour is called stagy, the sense of a showy, dramatic manner.

clue.text: Explain how lighter citizens of ancient city will have to conserve energy

parts.note: a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire

indicators.note: the citizens hold on to the energy letter

parts.note: the people of Thebes in ancient Greece
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An ancient city's people must save energy, and someone explains how they light fires.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reveal or disclose what was secret, a loose sense of making something clear.

clue.text: Robbers in group returned it after seizing it

indicators.note: the combination grabs the second it inside itself
the reversed word comes after the group

parts.note: a band is a group

indicators.note: returned means the first it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A gang returns loot after grabbing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'it's do different jobs: the first is turned round by 'returned', the second is the one seized. 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old plural of bandit, outlaws or brigands who rob people.

clue.text: Subordinate tax absorbing English pence

indicators.note: the tax takes in the two abbreviations

parts.note: a duty is a tax

explanation.surface: A lesser tax that swallows English pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command acts under and for a superior, so is a subordinate.

clue.text: Group of voices? Hard work fails to complete our group

indicators.note: the final letter of the task word is left off

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task
us refers to our group

explanation.surface: Our team finds the hard work too much to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of singers performing together is a choir or ensemble of voices.

clue.text: Drunk and tense before examination in seaside locale

indicators.note: the first pieces precede the examination word

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A student, drunk and nervous before an exam at the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the shore region of a sea or lake, a coastal zone.

clue.text: Scottish resident's done playing with a bairn

indicators.note: playing about with letters rearranges them, here done and a bairn

explanation.surface: A Scot has finished playing with a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges DONE and A BAIRN; 'with' only joins them. A bairn is Scots for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or inhabitant of the city of Aberdeen in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Neatly heeding decaying — addressing this?

indicators.note: something decaying falls apart, so the letters of neatly heeding are rearranged

explanation.surface: Carefully attending to rot is what tooth care is all about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decaying' rearranges NEATLY HEEDING; read whole, the clue describes the practice that tackles tooth decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Care of teeth and gums aims to prevent decay, so it is the practice that deals with rotting teeth.

clue.text: Tight-fisted girl's not a success

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A stingy girl is a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that narrowly fails to hit its target is a failure, though only just.

clue.text: Present Government touchy about university independence

indicators.note: the irritable word wraps around the two letters

parts.note: ratty means irritable

explanation.surface: The present government is prickly about university independence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like the time word but is a noun here: a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip given for service is a small gift of money.

clue.text: Search keeping a cool guy back in series of tunnels

indicators.note: the search word keeps the other pieces in front of it, at its back

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a cool man
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: A search party holds back a cool character in a tunnel network.
explanation.walkthrough: COMB keeps A CAT at its back, i.e. ahead of it, with the two words in the order CAT A.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground cemetery made of galleries is a network of passages.

clue.text: Ban Baron from contest over endless grassy area

indicators.note: in a down entry the first part sits over the second
the baron letter is taken from the contest word

parts.note: a bout is a contest or fight

indicators.note: the last letter of the grassy word is dropped

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass

explanation.surface: A nobleman is banned from a competition held on a shortened lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit something by law is to make it illegal, the verb sense.

clue.text: Lots of games are absorbing vulgar chap

indicators.note: the verb takes the cad inside it

parts.note: a cad is an ill-mannered man

explanation.surface: A boor gets wrapped up in lots of games.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement hall full of coin-operated machines holds many games.

clue.text: Pillar's a deception, concealing chimney

indicators.note: the trick hides the chimney inside it

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
lum is Scots and northern English for a chimney

explanation.surface: A stone pillar turns out to be a trick hiding a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright cylindrical support in architecture is a post or shaft.

clue.text: Rodent making cat and sheep turn tail

indicators.note: turning tail sends the pair of animal words backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A rodent makes a cat and a sheep flee.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing ground squirrel of mountain regions belongs to the order of gnawing mammals.

clue.text: I take in a yard open to the sky

indicators.note: I and the take letter go in the a-and-yard pair

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone moves into a yard with no roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A space that is light and breezy is open, exposed to fresh air and sky.

clue.text: Flight specialist not right about question regarding eagle

indicators.note: the shortened carrier goes around the question letters
the right letter is removed

parts.note: an airline specialises in flights

explanation.surface: An aviation company, wrong about a question concerning eagles.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or like an eagle, as in a hooked nose.

clue.text: Radio report's trashed lattes

parts.note: a cry is a report or shout; with the 's it gives cry's

indicators.note: trashed lattes have their letters wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A news report says coffees were thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: An early simple wireless receiver using a crystal detector is a kind of radio.

clue.text: Floating vegetation circling round quantity of water

indicators.note: the vegetation goes round the round letter

parts.note: a mat is a dense layer of floating weed
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Weed floating round a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive ditch filled with water around a castle holds a body of water.
